x: I, II and III are correct: solar and wind are renewable and coal is not. IV is false because petroleum is a non-renewable fossil fuel.
t: Sort the sources into renewable and non-renewable.

x: Option B is incorrect: nuclear energy uses uranium, a finite mineral, so it is non-renewable. Biomass and hydroelectricity are renewable, and petroleum is a non-renewable fossil fuel.
t: Sort each source into renewable or non-renewable.
o: Nuclear energy is a renewable source.

x: Both are true and R explains A: biomass is renewable because the plants and wastes it comes from regrow or are produced again quickly, unlike fossil fuels.
t: Check whether R gives the reason the source can be replaced.
s:
Assertion (A): Biomass is a renewable source.
Reason (R): Biomass comes from plant matter and animal wastes that are replenished within a short time.

x: Jatropha is a biodiesel crop, Pongamia (karanja) another biodiesel plant, sugarcane gives bio-ethanol, and solar uses photovoltaic cells. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each source to its fuel or technology.

x: The National Solar Mission, one of the NAPCC's eight missions, is the one for solar energy. Solar cells turn sunlight into electricity.
t: Match each mission to its source.

x: Natural gas is a non-renewable fossil fuel, hydroelectricity is renewable energy from flowing water, uranium is a non-renewable nuclear fuel and sugarcane is a source of bio-ethanol, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Classify each energy source by type.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Natural gas
(b) Hydroelectric energy
(c) Uranium
(d) Sugarcane

List-II
(i) Renewable energy from flowing water
(ii) Non-renewable fossil fuel
(iii) Non-renewable nuclear fuel
(iv) Source of bio-ethanol

x: SO₂ comes from fuel burning, power plants, diesel and smelters; NOx from transport and boilers; CO from vehicles and waste burning; and benzene from petrol. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each pollutant to its source.

x: Both are true: acid rain has a pH below 5.6, and SO₂ and NOx cause it. Its causes do not explain the 5.6 cut-off, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a cause explains a threshold.

x: Option C is incorrect: mahua and neem are biofuel (oil) sources, not ethanol crops. The ethanol crops are sugarcane and maize.
t: Discriminate biodiesel plants from ethanol crops.

x: All three are correct: SpiceJet flew India's first biofuel flight, from Dehradun to Delhi, on 27 August 2018.
t: Recall the first biofuel flight.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The first airline biofuel flight was operated by SpiceJet.
II. The first biofuel flight was on the Dehradun–Delhi route.
III. The date of the first biofuel flight was 27 August 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: bioremediation uses microbes to remove or break down pollutants, and heavy metals such as cadmium and lead poison many of those microbes, limiting the method.
t: Verify each statement on its own.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Bioremediation uses microorganisms to remove or detoxify pollutants.
Statement B: Heavy metals such as cadmium and lead are toxic to many microbes and limit bioremediation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: In a microbial fuel cell the catalysts are microbes, the substrate is organic matter, and one use is treating wastewater; algae for biofuel come from sea and land sources. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Match each part to its role.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: growing algae on non-farm land is an advantage, while the need for expertise, capital and large plants comes from the cost and complexity of cultivation and processing.
t: Ask whether R is an advantage or the cause of A.
s:
Assertion (A): Algae biofuel requires expertise, capital and large-scale facilities.
Reason (R): Algae can be grown on land that is unsuitable for agriculture.

x: A key limitation of biofuel is that it is not yet cost-effective compared with fossil fuels.
t: Recall the drawback of biofuels.

x: All three are correct: producer gas is a mix of CO, H₂, CO₂ and methane, and bio-asphalt is a renewable, non-petroleum building material.
t: Recall the bio-based materials.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Producer gas or synthetic gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and methane.
II. Bio-asphalt is a renewable construction material.
III. Bio-asphalt is a non-petroleum construction material.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All five are major sources of PM10 and PM2.5: combustion, construction, industry, diesel exhaust and road dust.
t: Recall the sources of particulate matter.

x: Both are true: ozone is a secondary pollutant because it forms in the air by photochemical reactions rather than being released directly. R explains A.
t: Discriminate primary from secondary pollutants.

x: PAHs come from incomplete combustion and industry, lead from leaded fuel and soil particles, ozone from photochemical reactions of NOx and hydrocarbons, and cadmium from metal production and smelting, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Link each pollutant to its main source.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs)
(b) Lead
(c) Ozone
(d) Cadmium

List-II
(i) Leaded fuel and soil-derived particles
(ii) Incomplete fuel combustion and industrial emissions
(iii) Photochemical reactions of NOx and hydrocarbons
(iv) Metal production and smelting

x: All four are correct: fuel burning, metal production, phosphate fertilisers and battery waste release cadmium, and pollution from human activity is called anthropogenic.
t: Verify each source of cadmium and the term anthropogenic.
s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Fuel combustion is a major source of cadmium pollution.
II. Metal production is a major source of cadmium pollution.
III. Phosphate fertilisers and battery waste are sources of cadmium pollution.
IV. Human-made pollution is called anthropogenic pollution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: sewage is biodegradable, while DDT, plastic and asbestos are not.
t: Sort pollutants by whether they break down.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Sewage is a biodegradable pollutant.
Statement B: DDT, plastic and asbestos are non-biodegradable pollutants.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: All four are correct: DDT, plastic and asbestos do not break down, and mercury builds up along food chains (biomagnification).
t: Recall which pollutants biomagnify.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. DDT is a non-biodegradable pollutant.
II. Plastic is a non-biodegradable pollutant.
III. Asbestos is a non-biodegradable pollutant.
IV. Mercury undergoes biomagnification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All three are correct: DDT and mercury biomagnify, so their concentration is highest in top predators.
t: Remember: biomagnification peaks at the top of the food chain.

x: CO binds haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin, SO₂ is a main cause of acid rain, ozone is a secondary pollutant from photochemical reactions and DDT is a non-biodegradable pesticide that biomagnifies, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Link each pollutant to its effect or nature.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Carbon monoxide (CO)
(b) Sulfur dioxide (SO₂)
(c) Ozone (O₃)
(d) DDT

List-II
(i) Forms carboxyhaemoglobin in blood
(ii) A main cause of acid rain
(iii) Secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions
(iv) Non-biodegradable pesticide that biomagnifies

x: PAN and smog are both secondary pollutants, formed in the air. CO, SO₂ and NOx are primary.
t: Discriminate primary from secondary pollutants.

x: Both are true: CO poisoning forms carboxyhaemoglobin because CO binds to haemoglobin. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the binding explains the result.

x: Both are true: photochemical smog needs sunlight because it forms when NOx and hydrocarbons react under sunlight. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the ingredients explain the condition.

x: Both are true: radiation can cause hereditary (genetic) changes and cancer.
t: Recall the effects of radiation.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Radioactive pollution causes hereditary changes.
Statement B: Radioactive pollution causes carcinogenesis.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: Chernobyl (Ukraine, 1986) was a nuclear accident that spread radioactive pollution.
t: Recall the Chernobyl disaster.

x: Nanoparticles pollute water and soil and enter the food chain.
t: Recall the effects of nanoparticles.
